items.title: Trifecta effect! How RIL, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank are powering Nifty rebound after 2 years
items.description: The Nifty has soared over 10% in November, heading for its best monthly performance in six years. Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank are powering the rebound, with their combined weight of nearly 28% making them critical to the index’s momentum. Can improving fundamentals sustain the rally?

items.title: Namaste Nifty, bye-bye AI trade? FIIs cross Rs 1 lakh crore monthly buying mark for the first time
items.description: Foreign investors have poured over ₹1.12 lakh crore into Indian equities in November, marking the strongest monthly inflow on record. The buying has reversed recent outflows, helped Indian markets outperform global peers and eased FII net selling for 2026 to around ₹1.8 lakh crore, amid signs of a slowdown in the global AI trade.

items.title: Star Health among 3 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On November 18, three Nifty500 stocks that gained over 5% appeared in the RSI Trending Up scan, according to StockEdge data. The signal is triggered when a stock’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) crosses above 50 from below, indicating strengthening price momentum. RSI is a technical indicator traders use to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: Tata Motors PV, Maruti Suzuki, and other auto stocks jump up to 4%. What’s driving the rally?
items.description: Auto stocks, including Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Maruti Suzuki and M&M, rallied on Thursday as copper, aluminium and other industrial metals slid to multi-month lows. The correction could ease raw-material cost pressures for automakers and support margins, although a stronger dollar and concerns over global demand drove the commodity sell-off.

items.title: Nifty flies 10% in a month; smallcaps going nowhere. Which stocks should you buy at this stage?
items.description: The Nifty has surged 10% in a month, but smallcaps have barely participated in the rally. Foreign investor inflows, softer crude oil prices and a global rotation away from AI stocks have boosted largecaps. Market experts weigh the valuations, earnings outlook and opportunities across largecap and smallcap stocks.

items.title: Sensex rises 150 points, Nifty above 25,250. Why analysts see potential for more uptrend?
items.description: The Indian stock market rebounded on Thursday with Sensex and Nifty recording gains after recent profit booking. Maruti Suzuki shares led the gains, while IT stocks faced losses amidst the trading activity. Analysts suggest the market may still see upward momentum due to sustained foreign institutional investments. Technical views predict fluctuations in Nifty, with potential for further downturns if certain levels are not maintained.

items.title: Red metal feels the blues! Voltas, Blue Star, other AC stocks jump up to 6% as copper prices hit 7-month lows
items.description: AC stocks such as Voltas, Blue Star and PG Electroplast rallied up to 6% as copper prices fell to a seven-month low. A stronger US dollar, concerns over Chinese demand and an AI-linked stock selloff weighed on the metal, while lower input costs supported appliance makers.

items.title: LT Foods share price rockets 8% after subsidiary acquires US’ Maya Kaimal in $6 million deal
items.description: LT Foods shares rallied on Thursday after its US subsidiary acquired MK Food Holdings for $5.8 million. The deal adds Maya Kaimal, a premium Indian-inspired foods brand, to its portfolio. Known for its sauces, curries and rice products, the brand will strengthen LT Foods' ready-to-eat offerings and US presence.

items.title: HAL, Bharat Dynamics, other defence stocks rise up to 3% as production hits fresh record high; ministry seeks 20% capex hike
items.description: Defence stocks gained after Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh said the ministry is targeting a 20% increase in capital expenditure in CAGR terms this year, following a 22% rise last year. With FY27 defence capex budgeted at Rs 2.19 lakh crore, the ministry plans to accelerate procurement and sign another record value of contracts.

items.title: IT stocks miss the November party despite FII comeback and cooling AI trade: What's holding back the sector?
items.description: Despite a market uptick fueled by foreign investments and solid corporate earnings, IT stocks are lagging behind. The Nifty IT index has experienced about a 4% decline in November following a robust 18% increase in October. This disparity indicates a disconnect between the overall market enthusiasm and the stagnant earnings for IT companies. Although artificial intelligence holds promise for future growth, it hasn't yet significantly impacted current revenues.

items.title: Paytm, MobiKwik, Pine Labs shares tumble up to 7% on reports of further UPI MDR delay. What's next?
items.description: Shares of Paytm, MobiKwik and Pine Labs fell after reports suggested that the rollout of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select UPI transactions could face further delays, potentially extending beyond the 2027 assembly elections in five states. The government is reportedly wary of a backlash from merchants and trade associations ahead of the polls.

items.title: Physicswallah shares jump 3% as firm targets 3x revenue surge to Rs 10,000 cr by FY30. How has stock performed since listing?
items.description: PhysicsWallah has set an ambitious FY30 revenue target of Rs 9,000-10,000 crore, banking on over 25% annual growth and improved profitability. The edtech firm also outlined its online-offline business mix and reported strong Q2 profit growth.

items.title: Morgan Stanley is ‘overweight’ on these 9 largecap stocks. How many do you own?
items.description: India offers durable, diversified, and decoupled growth – characteristics that will likely bring upside risks to Indian stocks if the AI capex story wanes and/or geopolitics settle down. In any case, India's earnings growth cycle is gaining traction. This is important because a principal catalyst for India to outperform in 2027 is how the market gauges the earnings growth gap between India and the world. Here are 9 stocks the brokerage is bullish on.

items.title: Sterlite Technologies among 3 stocks showing White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On November 19, three Nifty500 stocks appeared in StockEdge’s White Marubozu bullish scanner, according to the technical scan data.A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in which the opening price is the session's low and the closing price is the high. It appears as a long white or green candle with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow, indicating strong buying momentum during the session.

items.title: CreditAccess Grameen among 7 stocks closing below VWAP
items.description: On November 18, the closing prices of seven stocks from the Nifty 500 pack fell more than 1% below their respective VWAPs (Volume Weighted Average Prices), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. VWAP represents the average price at which a stock traded during the day, weighted by trading volume. A closing price below VWAP indicates that the stock ended the session below its volume-weighted average traded price.

items.title: HNIs now own a record Rs 10 lakh crore worth of Indian stocks. Laurus Labs, Cupid among top 10 favourites
items.description: In an impressive move, high net worth individuals (HNIs) have ramped up their investments, amassing a monumental ₹10 lakh crore in Indian equities. This surge is particularly evident within the healthcare and consumer discretionary sectors over the past quarter. While retail investors faced a sell-off, HNIs selectively bolstered their portfolios, with significant contributions from firms like Sun Pharmaceutical Industries and Laurus Labs, spotlighting the healthy performance across various sectors.

items.title: Fund managers turn overweight on India, first such classification since Jan
items.description: Fund managers have recently indicated an increased interest in investing in India after several months of cautious sentiment. A significant number of investors are concerned about the absence of artificial intelligence-related investment options available. Increased interest in healthcare and shifts toward defensive sectors have been noted, reflecting changing priorities among investors. Despite concerns over potential risks, half of the fund managers predict a soft landing for the global economy.

items.title: Fairfax-backed FIH Mauritius buys 11.8% stake in IIFL Capital Services for Rs 1,540 crore as promoters pare stake
items.description: FIH Mauritius Investments, a Fairfax Financial arm, acquired an 11.8% stake in IIFL Capital Services for Rs 1,540 crore through bulk deals. Promoters Nirmal Jain and Venkataraman Rajamani sold shares, while IIFL Finance also saw a major Fairfax stake sale.

items.title: NSE among 5 stocks hitting 52-week highs; stock rallies up to 27% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex climbed 990 points to settle at 83,021 on Thursday. Riding the market rally, five stocks from the BSE 200 index hit fresh 52-week highs, touching their highest price levels in the past 12 months. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the last year and may indicate heightened market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A commercial vehicle major for a 7.85% upmove, a large-cap auto stock for a 7% rise
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Investors vs Economists: Should Govt Cut LTCG Tax?
items.description: Investors and industry leaders are pushing for an LTCG tax cut to attract foreign capital, while economists want the current tax structure retained. With FIIs returning to Indian markets and equity LTCG emerging as a significant revenue source, will Budget 2027 deliver tax relief or stick to the status quo?

items.title: Sebi looks to tighten monitoring of issue proceeds, shifts focus to fund utilisation beyond fundraising
items.description: Sebi has proposed tighter monitoring of funds raised through public issues, including direct reporting by monitoring agencies to stock exchanges and extending oversight to issuances of all sizes, excluding OFS. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the move aims to strengthen corporate governance, improve transparency and protect investor interests while easing business processes.

items.title: Market wrap: Maruti Suzuki, Eicher Motors, TCS, Tech Mahindra top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian stock markets staged a strong recovery on Thursday, with Sensex rising 990 points and Nifty gaining 286 points. Maruti Suzuki led the gainers on both indices, surging 7.58%, while IT heavyweights TCS, Tech Mahindra and Infosys featured among the top losers. Here's a complete list of the session's movers.

items.title: NSE stock closes 5% higher amid renewed interest in large caps, 'buy' rating from brokerages; should you hold or sell?
items.description: NSE shares surged on Thursday to hit a fresh all-time high, extending their rally for a second consecutive session. The stock has gained 24% over its issue price, drawing renewed interest after brokerages initiated coverage with ‘buy’ ratings. Here are the key growth drivers and what investors should consider.

items.title: Reliance Industries share rebound is not over yet, says JPMorgan. Target price set at Rs 1,675
items.description: JPMorgan sees nearly 23% upside in Reliance Industries to ₹1,675, saying the stock’s recent rally of over 13% in a month has yet to reflect its improving earnings outlook. The brokerage maintained its overweight rating, expecting strong year-on-year profit growth over the next few quarters, led by the oil-to-chemicals business.

items.title: Why did market rise today? Sensex crosses 83,000 for first time since Iran war began; Nifty tops 25,500. 5 factors behind Rs 6 lakh cr gains
items.description: The stock market witnessed a robust recovery, with Sensex and Nifty climbing over 1%, resulting in a remarkable addition of nearly Rs 6 lakh crore to market capitalization. Key players like Maruti Suzuki and M&M facilitated the gains, while IT stocks stumbled. Notably, foreign investors have remained active net buyers for 13 straight sessions, accumulating more than Rs 1 lakh crore in November alone.

items.title: For long-term investors, with some patience: 5 large-cap stocks from different sectors with upside potential of up to 24%
items.description: There comes a point in the stock market when it is more important to manage risk than to take it. It is a lesson that is often forgotten when the market mood turns good, as it has now. The way to participate in such a market without getting hurt is to focus on businesses that earn well and have seen bad times before.

items.title: Anthropic @ $1.5 trillion: A 5-year-old AI company is now worth more than India Inc’s top 10 combined
items.description: Anthropic’s $1.5 trillion IPO valuation exceeds the combined market capitalisation of India’s top 10 listed companies by around 45%. The five-year-old maker of Claude is worth nearly 7.6 times Reliance Industries, raising questions about India Inc’s valuations and its ability to capture opportunities in the global AI boom.

items.title: Tata Chemicals shares jump 3%, up 10% in November so far as Tata Sons IPO buzz builds
items.description: Tata Chemicals shares gained as expectations of a Tata Sons IPO gathered pace after an RBI nudge. The stock touched Rs 653.90 on the NSE, taking its market capitalisation closer to Rs 16,500 crore. Tata Chemicals holds a 2.53% stake in Tata Sons, valued at around Rs 30,052 crore, making it a potential beneficiary of IPO-related sentimen

items.title: Private sector banks can grow 2x faster than PSU banks: Motilal Oswal
items.description: Private banks are expected to stage a strong earnings recovery over FY26-FY28, with profit growth projected to be twice that of PSU banks. Motilal Oswal expects stable credit momentum, liquidity deployment and lower stress in unsecured loans to support the turnaround.

items.title: Explained: 3 reasons why gold prices are stuck at a 14-month low and should you buy the yellow metal?
items.description: Gold prices remained near 14-month lows on Thursday despite oversold conditions and renewed Middle East tensions, as three major factors continued to outweigh safe-haven demand. Spot gold was little changed at $3,722.84 an ounce after touching $3,693.13, its lowest since September 2025

items.title: Goldman Sachs names 22 ‘high-growth’ stocks; Bharti Airtel, Eternal and HDFC Bank feature in the list
items.description: Indian equities have rallied over the past few weeks despite weakness in global markets. Falling crude oil prices and sustained foreign institutional inflows into Indian financial stocks have supported domestic markets, offsetting technology-led risk aversion in other markets, particularly South Korea and Taiwan.Against this backdrop, Goldman Sachs has identified 22 high-growth companies with exposure to structural growth themes and initiated Buy ratings on 21 of them.
